head_commit.message:
Authorise workspace cleanup by its preservation receipt, not by a lease the protocol has already ended

Every completed attempt preserved its Candidate and then died. The Runner
releases its lease as Succeeded before asking gitd to delete the workspace, and
that order is deliberate: it is pinned by a simulation test so that a crash
between the two leaves a recorded Candidate rather than a workspace nobody can
account for. But cleanup then took a Kernel mutation permit like any other
write, and minting one performs an online lease and fence read-back, which the
release has just made impossible. The Runner's own source called this a known
contradiction and said the resolution belonged here, because cleanup is
documented as receipt-gated.

Cleanup now proves itself with the sealed preservation receipt it is already
given. handle_cleanup verifies the session token, refuses a frozen daemon, and
calls the new PreservationAuthority::authorize_receipt before any reservation,
so the seal, the state digest, the cleanup target, the destination identity, the
artifact shape, the salvaged objects, the bundle and the artifact digest are all
checked first. It then reserves through authorize_by_preservation_receipt, which
computes the same transport fingerprint as the Kernel path and builds a complete
MutationSubject from the receipt digest, the operation and the session's exact
writer incarnation, but consults no online checker. Settlement is recorded in
the durable mutation ledger without a Kernel round trip, and an indeterminate
outcome still freezes the daemon. Every other operation keeps the Kernel permit
path unchanged, with its signatures untouched.

Exactly-once survives: a reservation replay returns the durable result rather
than a second permit, a replay whose recorded digest does not reproduce refuses
AUTHORITY_REPLAY_CONFLICT, and a second cleanup deletes nothing again.

Proof: 171 tests pass across bullet-gitd and bullet-git-workspace, 72 with all
features; clippy with -D warnings and rustfmt are clean. Eleven new tests cover
cleanup succeeding against a checker that can issue no permit while another
operation on the same daemon still refuses AUTHORITY_CONTRACT_UNAVAILABLE;
garbage, empty, byte-tampered and foreign-session receipts each refusing
PRESERVATION_RECEIPT_REFUSED while leaving the session usable and the real
receipt still working; replay behaviour; and a post-permit repository failure
still yielding MUTATION_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and freezing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_015qHQABNS382h2gi5jb5oUY

head_commit.message:
Pin an install-action that actually carries the tools CI asks for

The first GitHub Actions run this repository has ever had failed in the
fast, lint, contract and security lanes with

    install-action does not support cargo-nextest@0.9.137
    (fallback is disabled by 'fallback: none' input option)

The pinned v2.62.45 manifest predates the versions the lanes require, and
`fallback: none` is correct, so the pin was the thing to move. Bumped to
v2.87.9, whose manifests carry cargo-nextest 0.9.137, shellcheck 0.10.0
and zizmor 1.25.2. The requested tool versions are unchanged.
